name: Operation Invoker
description:
Invoke an operation or binding addressed by name in a supplied OpenBindings interface document. Caller selection identifies the intended binding; the operation's schemas describe the caller-facing values, and the kind of the selected binding's source gives the binding's data meaning.

These operations are offered for voluntary adoption by name. Their schemas and descriptions identify the exchanged values and the capability they describe; they do not prescribe an SDK, internal algorithm, validation or recovery policy, or process architecture. Correspondence is an author claim, not verification of an implementation.

BindingContext.description: Opaque context supplied by value for one attempt, as the context document defines it. Its members are whatever a previous challenge's schema described or the caller knows the source's kind reads; this interface defines none of them, requires no store, and prescribes no acquisition mechanism. How a value is used stays inside the kind's implementation. A value may be secret: a challenge marks secrets writeOnly, and callers avoid disclosing context through logs, diagnostics or storage keys.

ContextRequiredDetails.description: The data of a CONTEXT_REQUIRED error or a preflight result, as the context document defines it: why the attempt could not proceed, in the producer's words, and a JSON Schema of the context object to supply on the next attempt. The schema is ordinary JSON Schema 2020-12: oneOf branches with a title each for alternatives, required for values needed together, writeOnly on secrets, and a property description for where a person obtains a value. It describes the context requested for one attempt, not permission to disclose anything else. Acquisition, trust, storage and retry decisions belong to the caller.

message.description: Why the attempt could not proceed, in the producer's words, for a person to read.

schema.description: A JSON Schema 2020-12 schema, in object form, of the context object to supply on the next attempt. The context document defines the conventions it uses and the oauth2 annotation an application may act on.

InvocationError.description: Unsuccessful-completion record carried by an error frame. The frame kind signals failure independently of the code. Codes defined by the invocation interfaces retain their documented meanings; kind-defined codes have that kind's meaning, and other strings have implementation-specific meaning. ERR_REFUSED asserts no observable effect of the requested operation; CONTEXT_REQUIRED additionally carries the context challenge and asserts no operation output. ERR_EXECUTION_FAILED reports failure without a claim about effects, dispatch, blame, retryability or protocol category. Choosing whether to trust or act on an error is consumer policy.

code.description: Machine-readable reason. Binding invocation owns ERR_BINDING_NOT_FOUND (the requested key names no binding in the supplied interface), CONTEXT_REQUIRED (context requested, no operation output or effects), ERR_REFUSED (no operation effects), ERR_EXECUTION_FAILED (failure making no claim about effects or dispatch), ERR_FRAME_PROTOCOL (reported frame-exchange violation), ERR_TRANSPORT_CLOSED (transport ended before a terminal outcome), and ERR_CANCELLED (caller cancellation, with no rollback or external-stop claim). Operation invocation additionally owns ERR_OPERATION_NOT_FOUND (unresolved operation), ERR_BINDING_SELECTION_REQUIRED (ambiguous binding choice), ERR_OPERATION_VALIDATION_FAILED (value violates a declared schema), and ERR_SCHEMA_UNRESOLVED (validity could not be determined), and also reports ERR_BINDING_NOT_FOUND with a broader meaning (unresolved allowed binding). These meanings do not prescribe detection, recovery or precedence. Other codes have kind-defined or implementation-specific meanings.

data.description: Optional portable JSON data associated with the unsuccessful completion. A rule defining `code` may define its structure and semantics; otherwise, the source's kind may use it to preserve an opaque application-authored failure value. For CONTEXT_REQUIRED, this is a ContextRequiredDetails object. Presence is significant: an absent member means no portable associated value, while an explicit null is a present JSON null value. Statuses, headers, trailers, envelopes, raw debugging bytes, exception prose, stacks, and implementation evidence do not belong here unless they are themselves application data under an explicit governing rule.

OperationInvocationInput.description: Initial payload carried by invokeOperation's open frame: the interface to act on and which operation to invoke (optionally with an ordered selection of its bindings) or which specific binding, plus context.

operation.description: Operation name to invoke: an operation key or any of its aliases, resolved equally against the interface's flat identifier namespace (core §5.1). A binding is resolved by the caller's ordered selection or by sole-candidate inference; ambiguity is refused.

binding.description: Binding key to invoke; the operation is derived from it and selection is bypassed entirely. Mutually exclusive with operation and selection.

selection.description: The caller's ordered choice among the operation's bindings: binding keys in preference order. The first listed binding the invoker can act on is used. Every key must name a binding of the resolved operation; a key that does not, or a list naming none the invoker can act on, fails with ERR_BINDING_NOT_FOUND rather than falling back to an unlisted binding. Requires operation; mutually exclusive with binding.

OperationInvokerInputFrame.description: Caller messages: open introduces the invocation request, input carries a value and close ends caller input. The exchange begins with one open; close is optional when input or invocation has already ended. Repeated close has the same meaning. Handling messages outside the described exchange is implementation policy.

oneOf.title: open
oneOf.description: Open the invocation. MUST be the first frame on the input stream.

oneOf.title: input
oneOf.description: Write one input value to the operation. Validated against the operation's input schema.

oneOf.title: close
oneOf.description: Caller half-close: no further input values. It does not itself report operation completion. Repetition has the same meaning.

OperationInvokerOutputFrame.description: One frame from invokeOperation back to the caller. Same shape as the binding-invoker output stream: zero or more `output`/`input_closed` frames, then exactly one terminal `complete` or `error`. Each output is validated against the operation's output schema.

oneOf.title: output
oneOf.description: One output value from the operation.

oneOf.title: input_closed
oneOf.description: The invoked binding is no longer accepting input. This is not a terminal outcome; outputs may still follow. Handling subsequent caller frames is implementation policy.

oneOf.title: complete
oneOf.description: Terminal: the operation completed normally. MUST be the last frame.

oneOf.title: error
oneOf.description: Terminal: the operation failed. MUST be the last frame. Carries a structured InvocationError.

openbindings.operation-invoker.invokeOpe.description:
Invoke an operation or explicit binding from the supplied interface document, exchanging OperationInvokerInputFrame and OperationInvokerOutputFrame values. The frame meanings are those of binding-invoker.invokeBinding.

An operation name is resolved under the core key-and-alias rules; a binding refers to its operation by primary key. An explicit binding identifies that binding without fallback. The candidate set is the operation's bindings whose sources' kinds the invoker can act on. An ordered selection identifies the first supported binding in that list; its entries name bindings of the requested operation. With no explicit choice, a sole supported binding is selected; zero candidates is ERR_BINDING_NOT_FOUND and multiple candidates is ERR_BINDING_SELECTION_REQUIRED. These input meanings do not choose a ranking based on metadata or registration order.

Inputs forwarded to the selected binding and successful outputs relayed to the caller satisfy the operation's declared schemas where present, read under the core schema rules. ERR_OPERATION_VALIDATION_FAILED reports an established mismatch; ERR_SCHEMA_UNRESOLVED reports inability to determine validity. An absent schema makes no validation claim. Validation implementation, preparation timing, caching and admission of documents outside the described input are implementation choices. A later failure does not retract earlier delivered values or imply absence of effects.

After resolution, the same document and the selected binding's key drive binding invocation; the binding's data and its source's data, including absence versus null, retain their meaning. Context is forwarded without reinterpretation; kind-defined adaptation belongs to binding invocation. The implementation may compose a binding invoker or provide the behavior itself.

ERR_OPERATION_NOT_FOUND describes an unresolved operation name; ERR_BINDING_NOT_FOUND an unresolved binding choice, a broader meaning than binding invocation's; ERR_BINDING_SELECTION_REQUIRED a choice still needed. These and the two validation codes have no data shape defined here. Binding-invoker and kind-defined error meanings remain applicable. Error precedence on malformed documents and internal resolution algorithms are not specified.

openByOperation.description: An alternative opening frame for the illustrative text document. Choose one addressing form per invocation; subsequent input, output and terminal frames have the binding-invocation meanings.

count.description: Count Unicode code points in the input string.

openByBinding.description: An alternative opening frame for the illustrative text document. Choose one addressing form per invocation; subsequent input, output and terminal frames have the binding-invocation meanings.

count.description: Count Unicode code points in the input string.

openWithSelection.description: An alternative opening frame for the illustrative text document. Choose one addressing form per invocation; subsequent input, output and terminal frames have the binding-invocation meanings.

count.description: Count Unicode code points in the input string.

openbindings.operation-invoker.preflight.description: Resolve the requested operation or binding using the same addressing meanings as invokeOperation, then report its preflight result. A later invocation is a separate attempt. Report context requirements identifiable for a possible invocation, as ContextRequiredDetails, or null for no prediction. Preflight does not perform the requested operation, consume its inputs or produce its outputs. It is advisory: null is a valid result even when invocation will need context; invocation does not depend on prior preflight. An unsuccessful completion reports inability to answer; ERR_REFUSED additionally reports that the same request would be refused without operation effects. Acquiring what the selected binding's data and its source's data refer to, caching and other preparation are implementation choices under the source's kind.
